1) the ILK level in the heart was up-regulated in parallel with myocyte hypertrophy after myocardial infarction, 2) ILK level was down-regulated when heart function decompensated, 3) ILK gene delivery can preserve tissue angiogenesis and heart function during cardiac remodeling after infarction.

ILK expression was temporally increased in the heart in response to external load, which was beneficial for cardiac hypertrophy and function.

the pathophysiology of cardiac remodeling.
the molecular basis of cardiac adaptation to external load.

the impairment of ILK related angiogenesis involved in cardiac maladaptation after infarction.

ILK expression is increased in the non-ischemic myocardium after myocardial infarction, and the up-regulation of this kinase is associated with the beneficial angiogenesis to improve heart function during cardiac remodeling.
